regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 and ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, acting at different immune checkpoints to support T-cell activity against cancer. regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line metastatic squamous NSCLC in adults without sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan. Ipilimumab: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed. Paclitaxel: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. There are two planned doses. Carboplatin: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycle 1 lasts 42 days: nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 1; nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 22. These are the only two planned chemotherapy administrations. From Cycle 2, nivolumab is given on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1. Continue while appropriate until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Your team reviews the plan and may delay or stop treatment.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan. Ipilimumab: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed. Pemetrexed: Pemetrexed blocks enzymes needed to make DNA and RNA building blocks. Dividing cancer cells are affected, but healthy blood-forming and mouth-lining cells can also be injured. Prescribed folic acid and B12 reduce toxicity; do not omit them because pemetrexed is an antifolate. There are two planned doses in this regimen. Carboplatin: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops. Pemetrexed: Pemetrexed is an antifolate: it blocks several enzymes that cells use to turn folate-dependent materials into DNA and RNA building blocks. With fewer building blocks, cancer cells have more difficulty copying their genetic instructions and dividing. Healthy rapidly renewing tissues, including bone marrow and the mouth lining, can also be affected. That helps explain low blood counts and mouth soreness. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce toxicity; they are part of the treatment, not supplements to omit because the drug is an antifolate. Cisplatin: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that disrupt copying and repair, helping kill cancer cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Kidney, hearing and nerve effects are important; blood tests, symptom checks and prescribed hydration help the team manage risk.

drug_profiles.name: Cisplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Kidney injury, changes in salts in the blood, hearing damage and nerve symptoms are important risks. Extra fluids and electrolyte checks are part of treatment. There are two planned doses in this regimen.

drug_profiles.name: Pembrolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops.
